questions.text:
Find the least positive angle in degrees coterminal with  
\[
\frac{37\pi}{12}-845^\circ.
\]
A sector has perimeter \(20\) and central angle \(2\) radians. Find its area.
In a circle, the numerical value of the arc length of a sector equals the numerical value of the area of that sector. If the central angle is not \(0\), find it.

A point moves on a circle of radius \(6\) cm. In the first half of a trip it turns through \(150^\circ\); in the second half it turns through \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\) radians. Find the total distance traveled.

Two angles in standard position satisfy
\[
\alpha+\beta=7\pi,\qquad \alpha-\beta=250^\circ.
\]
Find the least positive coterminal angle of \(\alpha\).

A wheel of radius \(r\) rolls without slipping. After exactly \(9\) revolutions, the distance traveled equals the area of a sector of a circle of radius \(r\) and angle \(\theta\) radians. Find \(\theta\).

questions.source_label: Chapter 5.1 / Olympiad Problems / Gemini 3.1 Pro / Q1
questions.text: Find the smallest positive degree measure that is coterminal with an angle of exactly $1,000,000^\circ$.

questions.source_label: Chapter 5.1 / Olympiad Problems / Gemini 3.1 Pro / Q2
questions.text: A wire of fixed length $L$ is bent to form the complete boundary (two radii and an arc) of a circular sector. What central angle (in radians) maximizes the enclosed area of this sector?

questions.source_label: Chapter 5.1 / Olympiad Problems / Gemini 3.1 Pro / Q3
questions.text: Circle $A$ has a radius of $1$ unit and Circle $B$ has a radius of $2024$ units. If Circle $A$ rolls without slipping around the stationary, outer circumference of Circle $B$, how many full $360^\circ$ revolutions will Circle $A$ have completed about its *own* center by the time it returns to its exact starting position?

questions.source_label: Chapter 5.1 / Olympiad Problems / Gemini 3.1 Pro / Q4
questions.text: A single central angle $\theta$ is drawn within a pair of concentric circles, dividing the shape into a smaller inner circular sector and a surrounding outer annular region. If these two regions have the exact same area *and* the exact same perimeter, what is the value of $\theta$ in radians?

questions.source_label: Chapter 5.1 / Olympiad Problems / Gemini 3.1 Pro / Q5
questions.text: Assuming the Earth is a perfect sphere of radius $R$, a city on the equator travels through space at a linear speed $v$ purely due to the Earth's rotation. A second city, located perfectly due north of the first, travels at a linear speed of exactly $v/2$. What is the shortest distance along the Earth's surface between the two cities?

questions.source_label: Chapter 5.1 / Olympiad Problems / Gemini 3.1 Pro / Q6
questions.text: At 12:00, the minute and hour hands of a continuously moving clock perfectly overlap. Over the exact span of the next 12 hours, how many times will the angle between the two hands measure exactly $1$ radian?
